proposal: KEEP source-backed research baseline; ITERATE only explicitly listed unknowns within existing owners. No adoption or WIP promotion.

systems.scope: Default-branch develop snapshot; not a claim about the v3.6.0 release.

claims.claim: Claude plugin registers Stop, SessionEnd and PreCompact; Codex registers SessionStart, Stop and PreCompact. Python dispatch implements those four handlers. No prompt-submit or per-tool handler is in that dispatch. PreCompact calls transcript ingestion asynchronously (daemon wait=False or spawned miner), then synchronous project mining; a hook return is not proof the transcript finished persisting.
Prompt/tool capture through other adapters is not exhaustively audited; absence from this dispatch is not product-wide absence.

lesson.claim: Represent capture requests separately from durable-completion receipts.

claims.claim: The inspected Claude shell wrapper delegates to the shared Python hook runtime. That runtime advertises claude-code, codex and dsh; the two inspected manifests have different event coverage.
Legacy/manual hook setup and backup/backfill are documented separately.
Installer-wide idempotency, uninstall and rollback across Cursor/Antigravity/other integrations were not verified by reading these wrappers.

lesson.claim: Use thin adapters with explicit host capability tables and reversible owned configuration.

claims.claim: The README supplies a mempalace-recall skill for search-before-answer recall and scoped palace organization.
Inspected SessionStart initializes/probes readiness and emits empty output or a warning; it does not run retrieval. Stop output is a systemMessage or a legacy blocking save request.
No universal query-conditioned, pre-prompt injected packet is established by these hooks; recall skill compliance and other retrieval adapters were not executed.

lesson.claim: Distinguish skill-directed recall from deterministic automatic prompt injection.

claims.claim: Conversation exchange filing upserts text plus metadata. Stop periodically saves a compressed diary checkpoint from recent messages, requests transcript ingestion and may mine project files. Silent mode advances its save marker only when the diary reports a positive count; legacy blocking mode advances before agent-confirmed save.
The README verbatim emphasis describes conversation storage, not a guarantee that every diary/checkpoint is verbatim or that a checkpoint count proves all associated ingest jobs succeeded.

lesson.claim: Keep verbatim source capture and derived checkpoint summaries as separate representations.

claims.claim: Live exchange metadata includes source_file, chunk_index, authored_at, filed_at, ingest/extract modes, normalizer/chunker versions and source identity; the graph accepts source_closet, source_file, source_drawer_id and adapter_name.
A universal guarantee linking every derived checkpoint/triple to all exact original supporting turns was not verified. Source locators alone do not establish that guarantee.

lesson.claim: Carry source identity and derivation pointers without equating them to verified supporting-turn completeness.

claims.claim: Inspected paths include verbatim exchange drawers, compressed diary entries, and SQLite entity/triple graph structures. Backend base classes expose storage/retrieval interfaces.
Wings/rooms/drawers organize the source corpus.
Activation/KV, parametric learning and a persistent always-hot prompt are not established in this source sample.

lesson.claim: Preserve source, derived summary and graph as explicit views rather than inventing semantic drawers.

claims.claim: Backend registry supports entry-point discovery and configurable built-ins; base interfaces separate retrieval from storage implementation. Ranking combines vector similarity with candidate-corpus BM25.
README names ChromaDB as current default and local semantic recall; its benchmark headline was not reproduced.
No LLM-planner or cross-encoder guarantee is inferred from the inspected ranking module; graph availability does not establish graph expansion in every search.

lesson.claim: Backend abstraction and local hybrid retrieval are established controls, not novelty claims.

claims.claim: Exchange metadata separates authored_at from filed_at (authored_at falls back to filing time). Graph triples expose valid_from/valid_to and invalidate sets the end time; as-of filtering uses a half-open interval, with date-only compatibility handling.
These fields do not prove a complete bitemporal, append-only source revision ledger for every mutation.

lesson.claim: Separate source event time, ingestion time and interval validity with explicit boundary tests.

claims.claim: Search scoping is based on palace organization, with an agent recall skill.
Diary checkpoints are filed by agent and project-derived wing; readiness hooks are not a task-packet compiler.
Frozen, reusable, evidence-sufficient cross-subagent packets were not verified in the sampled sources.

lesson.claim: Treat recalled source excerpts and disposable task state as separately testable outputs.

claims.claim: Transcript spawns use per-target PID guards; write routing resolves once per hook burst. After attempted daemon submission, exceptions do not trigger a duplicate direct write. Require mode blocks writes if the daemon is unavailable and does not cold-start it.
The routing page explicitly labels this develop behavior unreleased and says v3.6.0 does not consume write_routing.hooks. First embedding use needs a model download.
CPU-storm resistance, crash recovery and secret-redaction completeness were not runtime-tested. Windows SessionEnd handling is described in code as best-effort without Windows CI coverage.

lesson.claim: Test ambiguous submission and retry receipts before copying any single-flight pattern.

systems.scope: Separately inspect OSS Memory SDK, coding-plugin shared core/Claude adapter, and Platform v3 documentation.

claims.claim: Claude manifest registers SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, Stop, PreCompact, SessionEnd and scoped sidekick subagent start/stop. Adapter routes failed tools and transcript-aware Stop into shared orchestration; pre-compact/session-end trigger flush.

lesson.claim: Normalize each event without implying every event must retrieve or admit memory.

claims.claim: Shared Python runner handles capture/search/flush; Claude adapter supplies transcript parsing and sidekick events. Manifest sets short per-event timeouts. Entrypoint logs exceptions and exits zero.
Claude is the audited installed-manifest path; other harnesses and installer/uninstaller/rollback guarantees were not verified. Shared-core naming alone is not proof of equal harness support.

lesson.claim: Centralize orchestration but retain adapter-specific transcript and protocol handling.

claims.claim: Runner searches only on the first recorded prompt, with a default 20-character minimum, query capped at 6000 characters, top_k=5 and a two-second search timeout argument. Results become UserPromptSubmit additionalContext. Shared core applies repository/directory/personal scopes and tracks previously injected memory IDs; default formatted-context budget is 4000 characters.
This is bounded retrieved memory text, not a verified minimum-sufficiency compiler.

lesson.claim: Budget and scope automatic retrieval; do not describe first-prompt recall as every-prompt recall.

claims.claim: Plugin records prompts, tool previews and assistant/transcript evidence locally, groups event ranges into flush packets and sends scoped extraction messages with infer=True to Platform v3. OSS infer=True uses existing-memory context, a single additive extraction call, batch embedding and hash dedup; infer=False stores message content directly.
The issue initial ADD/UPDATE/DELETE-loop hypothesis is too broad for this pinned default additive OSS path; explicit update/delete APIs and platform behavior must be evaluated separately.

lesson.claim: Separate local raw event capture, extraction requests and acknowledged durable memory.

claims.claim: SQLite EvidenceStore keeps timestamped repo/session event payloads, flush event ranges, packet IDs and remote semantic event IDs. Claude transcript parser follows the active conversation branch. Tool previews are bounded/redacted; this is not a byte-for-byte archive of all tool results.
Local flush provenance does not establish that every Platform-derived fact returns exact supporting-turn IDs. That server-side contract was not inspected.

lesson.claim: Retain local event-to-flush lineage while checking remote fact-to-turn support explicitly.

claims.claim: OSS path has memory text/metadata, embeddings, entity linking and message/history storage. Coding plugin separately keeps local evidence and structured extraction inputs; remote memories can be project or personal.
Activation/KV and parametric memory are not established here; neither raw-source absence nor platform graph behavior follows from the OSS main.py sample.

lesson.claim: Compare source and extracted views at the same product layer.

claims.claim: Current OSS search combines vector, BM25 and entity signals, with optional configured reranker; VectorStoreFactory selects the store. The plugin invokes the Platform search API rather than this local SDK retrieval pipeline.
Managed Platform ranking internals and equal quality across stores were not verified; no vector vendor is selected for TESSERA.

lesson.claim: Use version-specific hybrid-retrieval controls and separate optional reranking cost.

claims.claim: OSS memory has created_at/updated_at, change history and optional expiration_date filtering; plugin events/flushes have ingestion timestamps.
Platform v3 temporal reasoning ranks by extracted event dates and supports search reference_date; the pinned page explicitly excludes the OSS SDK.
A Graphiti-equivalent validity/invalidation interval contract is not established for the audited OSS path.

lesson.claim: Distinguish search-time temporal boosts from fact validity and supersession.

claims.claim: First-prompt additionalContext is assembled from retrieved memories. Shared core records injected memory IDs and sidekick runs; adapter injects sidekick context on the scoped subagent-start event.
A frozen cross-subagent packet with source-version validation and evidence-sufficiency semantics is not verified by these handoff records.

lesson.claim: Budgeted injection and subagent handoff need separate invariants from reusable frozen packets.

claims.claim: SQLite uses WAL/busy_timeout and BEGIN IMMEDIATE for flush preparation and duplicate Stop serialization. Atomic handoff renaming, stale-running recovery, limited relaunches, pending expiry and capped flush attempts bound retries. No API key yields local-only; redaction patterns and 0600 cached-key writes exist.
These mechanisms improve bounded recovery but expiry/gave-up states mean capture is not an unconditional remote durability promise. Regex redaction is not a complete secret-leak guarantee.

lesson.claim: Fail-open must expose local-only, retrying and gave-up states rather than imply saved.

systems.scope: Cloud CLI native-hook adapters and OSS MemOS runtime/MemCube are distinct codebases; backend service parity is unverified.

claims.claim: Cloud CLI maps search/add phases: Codex/Claude/Trae UserPromptSubmit→Stop; Hermes pre_llm_call→post_llm_call; Cursor beforeSubmitPrompt→afterAgentResponse; Cline UserPromptSubmit→TaskComplete; Copilot userPromptTransformed→agentStop; OpenCode chat.message→session.idle; OpenClaw before_prompt_build→agent_end; Antigravity PreInvocation→Stop; DeepSeek agent/pre-step→agent/turn-stopping.
Dedicated session-start, tool-event and pre-compaction capture are not established by this two-phase registry.

lesson.claim: Map host events to semantic phases while retaining host-specific coverage.

claims.claim: HookAgentSpec defines host event aliases, config/response style and installation mode. Installer removes owned stale entries and atomically writes configuration; uninstall targets managed hooks/plugins. JS/Python/file-hook adapters coexist with shared runner.
Multi-file transactional rollback and preservation under concurrent external settings edits are not proved by individual atomic writes; installations were not executed.

lesson.claim: Treat event normalization, installer ownership and output protocol as separate contracts.

claims.claim: Runner saves pending prompt state, searches configured backend with user/conversation scope (agent scope only for multi-view), and converts results to host-specific context. Cursor explicitly disables search injection while keeping prompt capture. Other outputs include additionalContext, modifiedTransformedPrompt, ephemeralMessage, contextModification or prependContext.
OSS MOS.chat independently searches accessible memory cubes and builds the system prompt before generation.

lesson.claim: Document hosts that can capture prompts but cannot inject retrieved memory.

claims.claim: CLI consumes saved turn state, combines user prompt and final assistant answer, and calls backend.add_memory(async_mode=True). Cancelled turns are skipped; missing final text can restore pending state. Antigravity waits for fullyIdle.
OSS tree memory add delegates to its memory manager, while MOS can submit scheduler messages when enabled.
Cloud service admission/dedup/extraction internals are not established by the OSS memory manager interface.

lesson.claim: Do not confuse asynchronous remote acceptance with durable completion.

claims.claim: OSS SourceMessage can hold role, chat_time, message_id, snippet, document path and file metadata; tree-memory metadata has multiple sources, file_ids and session identity. The CLI forwards a user/assistant pair and conversation scope.
Optional source fields do not prove a complete raw transcript archive or that every cloud-derived memory receives exact turn provenance.

lesson.claim: Make provenance optionality explicit and verify population, not only schema availability.

claims.claim: GeneralMemCube loads/dumps configured text, activation, parametric and preference-memory components; uninitialized backends remain absent. Tree metadata distinguishes working, long-term, user, tool, raw-file, skill and other memory types.
MOS activation use is gated to HuggingFace backends and consumes a KV-cache memory when configured.
The CLI does not demonstrate all these OSS modalities being active in its managed backend.

lesson.claim: Memory-type extensibility is distinct from TESSERA semantic drawers.

claims.claim: OSS TreeTextMemory wires graph store, embedder, optional strategy-controlled BM25, reranker and extractor LLM; search delegates fast/fine behavior to a searcher, and subgraph search exposes embedding or fulltext modes.
Cloud CLI simply calls backend search; its live vector store, reranking and planning stack are not proven to match OSS tree configuration.

lesson.claim: Separate configurable retrieval composition from claims of default production quality.

claims.claim: OSS metadata exposes created_at/updated_at, version, status, evolve_to, history, working_binding and archived-memory pointers. Archived records have optional timespec and state/event form; SourceMessage has chat_time. CLI pending turn state has created_at and a default 24-hour TTL.
This schema audit does not validate all update paths or establish Graphiti-equivalent interval semantics in Cloud CLI.

lesson.claim: Version-history schemas need mutation-path tests before becoming preservation guarantees.

claims.claim: MOS builds a system prompt from retrieved memories plus chat history, with optional scheduler and activation-cache paths. CLI formats ephemeral host context; Cursor injection is disabled. WorkingMemory metadata and working_binding exist in the OSS model.
Frozen reusable task packets with minimum-sufficiency checks are not established by these APIs.

lesson.claim: Evaluate context construction and scheduling without adopting a whole memory operating system.

claims.claim: Hook state uses 0700 directories, 0600 atomic writes, session/turn hashed keys, TTL cleanup and atomic consume. Runner logs failures and continues. Remote add happens after consume; network-save failures do not restore that state (missing final text does).
Atomic consume reduces duplicate callback submissions but leaves a crash/network-loss window before durable remote acknowledgement; fail-open is not durable delivery.
End-to-end secret redaction, provider retries and offline durability beyond pending state were not verified.

lesson.claim: Test the loss/duplicate boundary between local atomic claims and remote submission.

systems.scope: Active letta-code snapshot. The letta repository main is a pointer; the V1 server is historical on archive.

claims.claim: Current types define SessionStart/End, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PreCompact, Stop, SubagentStop, PermissionRequest and Notification. Executor supports command hooks and supported prompt hooks.
The agent prompt describes automatic recall-history storage and background reflection; those descriptions are instructions, not verification of every persistence path.

lesson.claim: Keep runtime hook availability distinct from automatic memory capture implementation.

claims.claim: Letta Code owns hook types and execution; config supports disabled hooks and matcher-based tool events. MemFS separately installs Git pre-commit validation and post-commit mirroring hooks.
Current README points to its terminal/App Server/desktop/web/channel surfaces.
Claude-compatible type naming does not establish cross-harness installation or uniform uninstall/rollback semantics.

lesson.claim: A native harness can expose familiar hooks without being an external wrapper.

claims.claim: Root MemFS Markdown files form core system-prompt memory; indexed child files and attached shared memory remain external. Prompt directs agents to recall/search missing history; recall is not automatically injected. Changes affect a later recompile, not the running turn.
Filesystem setup seeds root memory, initializes local/remote MemFS and explicitly invokes agents.recompile after enabling the remote git-memory tag.
This sample does not prove automatic query-specific retrieval on every prompt.

lesson.claim: Always-hot core context and retrieval-on-demand are distinct controls for a context compiler.

claims.claim: commitMemoryWrite stages specified paths, commits them, and returns committed/SHA; local mode and remote preparation paths are distinct. Git pre-commit validates memory layout/frontmatter and protected read-only fields. Post-turn sync is handled separately.
Prompt directs selective agent-owned updates and describes memory-worker worktrees/reflection.
Semantic correctness/dedup of every agent-written fact is not guaranteed by structural validation.

lesson.claim: Separate agent-authored memory, validation, local commit and remote sync.

claims.claim: MemFS Git commits and paths preserve inspectable file revisions; sync code reports dirty/unpushed state and can preserve a backup ref before specific unrelated-history recovery.
Recall history is described as immutable and automatically stored separately from editable memory.
Exact supporting-turn linkage for each authored memory and complete recall persistence were not verified in the sampled implementation.

lesson.claim: Git derivation history is valuable but does not replace claim-to-source-turn evidence.

claims.claim: Current prompt separates recall experience, root core memory, indexed external files, skills and attached shared-memory repositories.
Filesystem scaffolding, root block initialization, rendering limits and Git-memory preparation are implemented.
KV/activation or parametric-learning guarantees are not inferred from this prompt/file architecture; the retired V1 server is not current implementation evidence.

lesson.claim: Compare always-hot, external and historical memory without importing another system taxonomy.

claims.claim: Current prompt recommends grep/file search and a recall subagent.
MemFS code supplies bounded directory-tree rendering and Git-backed local projection.
The active runtime recall vector store, lexical/vector fusion, graph ranking, reranker and LLM query-planner implementation were not audited; V1 archival-vector claims cannot fill these gaps.

lesson.claim: Compare filesystem/recall behavior at the pinned active runtime, not remembered V1 architecture.

claims.claim: Git commits identify memory revisions; sync tracks pending commits and recovery history.
Prompt says memory changes take effect on later recompile and suggests inspecting history with Git.
Per-fact event/reference time, valid_from/valid_to and semantic supersession are not established for the audited MemFS path.

lesson.claim: Versioned memory history is not equivalent to event-time truth intervals.

claims.claim: Current-turn prompt remains compiled while edits prepare future state. Forked agents may inherit context, and memory workers use private worktrees. Shared memory is dynamically attachable and external to core prompt.
Explicit recompile calls and bounded memory-tree projection exist.
No evidence-sufficiency score, minimum-sufficient task packet or equivalent immutable evidence manifest was verified. Prompt-level policy is not proof all subagent snapshot semantics hold.

lesson.claim: A compiled prompt snapshot is a relevant control; do not claim frozen context itself as novel.

claims.claim: Hook executor uses timeouts, TERM then KILL, mapped exit codes and sequential/blocking versus parallel non-blocking execution. Git code retries classified transient errors, serializes config writes through a helper, redacts auth text, supports local-only writes and reports pending/conflicted sync. Some remote modes configure repository-local credential helpers.
No exhaustive process-storm, offline-sync or credential-exposure audit was run; configuring a helper is not proof that secrets never reach local Git config.

lesson.claim: Expose sync failures and scope credentials instead of treating commits as delivery.

systems.scope: Open-source core plus its MCP integration; no managed Zep backend equivalence is assumed.

claims.claim: Graphiti exposes add_episode; MCP add_memory queues an episode with text/message/JSON source, scope and reference_time. The inspected MCP tools are calls, not host SessionStart/Prompt/Tool/PreCompact/Stop subscriptions.
Automatic lifecycle coverage in managed Zep or other client integrations is outside this source sample.

lesson.claim: Treat explicit episode ingestion as a separate integration choice from automatic host hooks.

claims.claim: MCP server exposes search/ingest tools and scoped queue processing.
README describes HTTP/stdio and Claude Desktop/Cursor client configuration plus Cursor rules.
Host-hook installer idempotency, uninstall/rollback and cross-client event guarantees were not verified; managed Zep hooks are not inferred.

lesson.claim: MCP tools and client instructions are not automatic lifecycle delivery.

claims.claim: Core search returns structured nodes/edges/episodes/communities according to configured searches and filters; MCP exposes search_nodes and search_memory_facts scoped by group.
MCP instructions guide the agent to search for context.
Neither an MCP tool definition nor those instructions proves retrieval runs before every reasoning step or injects a precompiled task packet.

lesson.claim: Preserve structured search evidence; make application-controlled invocation explicit.

claims.claim: add_episode orchestrates extraction, node/edge resolution and graph persistence; edge operations call LLM-based resolution/temporal extraction. MCP add_memory returns queued-for-processing after enqueue.
Queue worker logs processing exceptions and marks tasks done; this is not a synchronous durable-write receipt.
No benchmark of extraction correctness or provider failure recovery was run.

lesson.claim: Distinguish queued acknowledgement, extraction, graph resolution and committed result.

claims.claim: EpisodicNode stores raw content, source/source_description, reference validity time and entity-edge IDs; EntityEdge lists originating episode IDs. Core store_raw_episode_content defaults true but can erase content before persistence when disabled.
Episode references do not alone guarantee exact original turn spans or retained raw content under every configuration.

lesson.claim: Episode-backed graph provenance is an established baseline for lineage experiments.

claims.claim: Models represent episodes, entities, fact edges, community nodes and saga state; facts/edges carry embeddings and provenance.
Activation/KV, parametric memory and always-hot core prompts were not established in these core/MCP paths. Managed Zep may have additional representations.

lesson.claim: Graph summaries and episode evidence must stay distinguishable in memory responses.

claims.claim: Search configuration dispatches BM25/fulltext, cosine similarity and BFS graph expansion; selectable rerankers include RRF, MMR, node distance, episode mentions and cross-encoder. Query embedding is computed only when configured methods need it.
MCP README supports graph-database/provider configuration, including Neo4j/FalkorDB paths and local Ollama setup.
No TESSERA vector store choice or quality ranking follows from those supported backends.

lesson.claim: Treat hybrid graph retrieval and selectable reranking as established controls.

claims.claim: Episode created_at is ingestion time and valid_at carries source/reference time. Entity edges include created_at, valid_at, invalid_at, expired_at and reference_time. Invalidation updates invalid_at and expired_at on old edges rather than inherently deleting them; optional raw content and explicit deletion APIs remain separate.
History-preserving invalidation is not an immutable-history guarantee against explicit deletion or changed retention settings.

lesson.claim: Use ingestion/event/validity/invalidation distinctions as temporal test controls.

claims.claim: Search returns configurable structured results. Episode ingestion can use prior episodes as context; saga/community summaries are graph state.
An always-hot agent prompt or disposable/frozen minimum-sufficient packet across subagents is not established in these core/MCP sources; Zep Context Lake claims were not audited.

lesson.claim: Retrieved graph context is not interchangeable with a frozen evidence-sufficient work packet.

claims.claim: MCP queue uses in-memory asyncio queues per group; worker exceptions are logged and tasks marked done. Worker-running flag is set inside the launched task, not atomically at enqueue. Core search uses semaphore_gather.

Queued acceptance is not restart-safe durable delivery in this queue implementation. Back-to-back enqueue before worker start warrants a race test; sequential intent is not a proved single-flight guarantee.
README warns that ingestion fans out into multiple provider calls and documents concurrency tuning and provider credentials.
No concurrency race, offline behavior, crash test or security audit was executed.

lesson.claim: Audit queue durability and worker ownership independently of advertised sequential processing.
